title: Savitri, the clever princess.
lines: This is an old story from India.
Long ago there lived a princess.
Her name was Savitri.
She was beautiful, but most of all very clever and kind.
Her father said: Savitri, you may choose who you marry yourself.
Go on a journey and look around.
Savitri travelled through the land.
In a forest she met a young man.
His name was Satyavan.
He was chopping wood for his old parents.
His father was blind.
He took very good care of them.
Satyavan was honest, kind and hard-working.
Savitri knew straight away.
He's the one I want to marry.
But there was a wise man at the court.
He said: Savitri, be careful.
In one year Satyavan will fall ill and leave this world.
It is written in the stars.
Savitri went quiet.
But she said: I have chosen.
I will marry him.
And I will take care of him.
They got married.
Savitri went to live in the forest.
In a simple little hut.
She cooked and took care of Satyavan's parents.
She was happy.
The year went by.
On the last day Satyavan went to chop wood.
Savitri went with him.
Under a big tree Satyavan got tired.
He laid his head on her lap.
He closed his eyes.
Then a big man in dark clothes came.
He had a rope in his hand.
It was Yama.
He had come to take Satyavan.
Yama walked away with Satyavan.
But Savitri followed him.
Go back, Savitri, said Yama.
This is my task.
But Savitri kept following.
She talked kindly and wisely with Yama.
About being good.
About being loyal.
About taking care of each other.
Yama thought her words were so beautiful.
You may make a wish, he said.
But not for Satyavan's life.
Savitri said: I wish that Satyavan's father could see again.
All right, said Yama.
But now go back.
Savitri kept following.
She kept talking.
Yama gave her a second wish.
And then a third.
With the third wish Savitri was clever.
She said: I wish to have many children.
Satyavan's children.
Yama said yes.
And then he understood.
For that wish to come true, Satyavan had to stay alive!
Yama laughed.
You are the cleverest person I have ever met.
He let go of the rope.
Satyavan was free.
Savitri walked back to the tree.
Satyavan opened his eyes.
I've been asleep for a long time, he said.
They walked home together.
Satyavan's father could see again.
Everyone was happy.
And women in India still celebrate a festival for Savitri.
To celebrate that love, loyalty and cleverness are very strong.
The end.
